title: Logo critique: inspect relationships
body: Silhouette: what reads before the details?
Interior spaces, curves and spacing shape the word.
Compare the full name and a compact mark.
Separate craft observations from personal taste.
notes: A useful critique names a visible relationship and the context in which it matters. Start with the overall silhouette, then inspect the spaces inside letters, the gaps between them, curve transitions and relative visual weight. These are proposed teaching checks, not a transcript of Lucy Eden's complete method. Her services page treats the primary logo, secondary version, smaller mark, typography, color and supporting artwork as one identity. That supports evaluating a family of related assets instead of asking a single logo to do every job. An exercise is to compare an unchanged wordmark in a broad header and a small square, noting which details disappear. Record observations before proposing changes. Readability, recognition and commercial impact are different questions; a cleaner drawing alone does not prove increased sales.
suggested_visual: Original annotated specimen using a neutral invented word: label silhouette, counter, spacing and curve; show wide-header and small-square contexts. Explicitly label as teaching diagram, not Lucy's work.

title: Lucy Eden: refine the existing letter
body: Bluey sample: vector anchors on the curved Y.
A comparison outline makes contour differences visible.
Small changes can retain a mark's character.
Evidence: sampled frames, not a complete critique transcript.
notes: The lead agent inspected Lucy Eden's public TikTok profile and sampled frames of the Bluey critique in the user's Chrome session on 8 September 2026. The player showed a runtime of one minute and twelve seconds. One editing frame showed vector anchors on the curved Y, a comparison outline and the on-screen word 'consistent.' This supports a narrow but valuable lesson: the work includes contour refinement within an existing letterform, rather than merely selecting a replacement font. It does not establish every change Lucy made, the full rationale or a measured improvement in recognition. Full audio and every before-and-after frame were not inspected. For practice, identify an inconsistent curve and compare one controlled adjustment while preserving the surrounding letters. This exercise is ours, not an attributed reconstruction of her complete process.
suggested_visual: Use the saved sampled editing frame if available, credited to Lucy Eden and Bluey; highlight the Y anchors without recreating an unobserved final result. Otherwise use a clearly labelled original contour-comparison diagram.

title: Michelle Elman: compose one unified name
body: Custom signature lettering nests into a unified arrangement.
A small speech bubble adds contextual character.
Patterns and illustrations carry additional expression.
Judge the composition against the intended personality.
notes: Lucy Eden's own Michelle Elman case study describes a rebrand intended to express candid, empathetic, bold and wise traits. She explains the primary mark as custom signature-style lettering arranged to nest together, with a speech-bubble detail above the i. The educational point is the division of labor: the name remains one recognizable composition while a restrained detail and supporting illustrations communicate additional context. This is the designer's stated rationale, not independent proof of how audiences perceive the mark. Ask where the letters share a rhythm, which gaps feel deliberate and whether the small detail still works at reduced size. Do not infer that every personal brand needs handwriting or a speech bubble. The transferable decision is to connect a particular identity to a particular construction, then test its intended uses.
suggested_visual: One credited primary wordmark from the case study beside a supporting-pattern example; annotate nesting and speech-bubble detail only after visually confirming the assets.

title: Splatter: let the experience shape the letters
body: Paint-throwing experience → bold, playful letter behavior.
Custom wordmark uses slanted and stacked forms.
A condensed badge adapts the identity to another space.
Real painted splashes become original supporting graphics.
notes: The Splatter case study links a paint-throwing experience to an identity intended to feel creative, liberating, edgy and fun. Lucy describes custom slanted and stacked letterforms and a condensed variation arranged as a symmetrical badge. She also describes painting on paper and scanning the results to make the pattern and icon material. That primary account establishes the maker's stated process; it does not make surface roughness a general test for human authorship. The lesson is to connect the behavior of the letters and supporting marks to the activity itself. Compare the expressive wordmark with its compact version: what remains identifiable when the arrangement changes? Originality can come from a specific process and a coherent set of choices, rather than from adding unrelated decorative effects to an otherwise conventional layout.
suggested_visual: Credited wordmark, badge and scanned-paint examples in three coordinated panels; caption the documented making process and avoid implying the teaching deck created these assets.

title: Marlowe & Sage: repeat a distinctive relationship
body: Rounded serif lettering supports the intended warmth.
An intertwined ampersand connects the full name.
The compact mark reuses initials and that connection.
A type category alone cannot determine personality.
notes: For Marlowe & Sage, Lucy's case study describes a childcare brand seeking a nurturing, warm, wise and encouraging presence. Her stated solution uses rounded serif lettering, with an ampersand woven into the wordmark. The smaller mark recombines initials through the same ampersand relationship, while simple shapes, leaves and light illustration support the wider identity. This is a useful counterexample to the blanket claim that serif typography must feel formal or dated. The actual construction and context matter. The practical exercise is to trace one distinctive relationship through the full wordmark and smaller mark, then ask what survives when detail is reduced. Do not copy the ampersand as a formula. Study the coherence between assets and evaluate the designer's intended warmth as a hypothesis rather than a measured audience response.
suggested_visual: Show credited primary and compact marks side by side with a connector tracing the repeated ampersand relationship; small supporting-pattern swatch below.

title: TBWA / DXD: making becomes a system
body: TBWA documents drawing, painting, cutting and experimentation.
The process supplies varied visual material.
A system still needs recognizable forms and clear hierarchy.
Maker process is documented; audience effects are not.
notes: TBWA's own public post states that its global design studio DXD used drawing, painting, cutting and experimentation while developing the new identity. That is primary corroboration of the studio's stated hands-on process. It does not prove that audiences trust rough imagery more, nor that all irregular marks were individually handmade. The teaching distinction is between generating material and organizing its use. A coherent system can allow variation in edges, annotations or image treatment while retaining identifiable shapes, legible typography and a clear order of information. Those proposed system checks are our synthesis; they are not an extracted TBWA rulebook. When reviewing the example, ask which visual qualities recur across applications and which change. The news index dates the DXD rebrand item to 5 August 2026; do not invent a broader historical origin from that one launch.
suggested_visual: Credited TBWA/DXD process frame beside two verified applications if available. Label 'documented process' separately from 'our questions about consistency and variation'; do not fabricate brand guidelines.

title: Anthropic: warmth and technical structure together
body: Geist connects the identity to human values and technical craft.
Typographic mark, Styrene/Tiempos and warm color work together.
Illustration extends the language for varied audiences.
A UI component system carries the identity into use.
notes: Geist's Anthropic case study describes more than an illustrative style. Its account connects a human-centered mission with technical craft through a typographic logo containing a distinct slash, the Styrene and Tiempos families, warm color, illustration and photography. It also describes an extensive UI component system and modular CMS. This offers a concrete example of a brand language extending into interface and product contexts. The educational question is how expressive qualities survive when the design must organize articles, controls and repeated content. The source is the studio's account of its project, not a current audit of every Anthropic surface. Its statements about AI safety, fundraising and company success are outside the design evidence used here. Neither warmth nor illustration alone demonstrates trust; the documented strength is the coordinated scope of the identity and implementation.
suggested_visual: Four credited case-study samples: typography, color, illustration and UI. Draw a simple connection from foundations to applications; do not use current product screenshots as if they were the historical deliverable.

title: Naive design: useful hypothesis, limited proof
body: Signals proposes hand-drawn character as a response to polished sameness.
Irregular appearance cannot prove human authorship.
McLuhan references and 'exponential trust' are not measurements.
Keep expressive material; test clarity and real applications.
notes: The user supplied a Signals transcript discussing deliberately hand-drawn design through TBWA/DXD, Who Gives A Crap, Oatly and Anthropic. The research record treats it as supplied text; this contributor did not independently watch or authenticate the complete clip. Its claims about AI perfection being ignored by the brain, form always preceding content, and trust increasing exponentially require evidence beyond portfolio examples. A McLuhan reference provides an interpretive perspective, not a controlled perception experiment. Oatly's own investor document dates its Nordic rebrand to 2013–14, so that example cannot establish that this entire approach originated in response to recent generative AI. The useful working hypothesis is that expressive material may help differentiate an appropriate identity. Evaluate coherence, reading and application separately, and preserve actual making records when provenance matters. No trust increase or Levarum direction is established by this research.
suggested_visual: Evidence matrix with three columns: creator interpretation, source-supported process, untested outcome. Include the Oatly 2013–14 timeline fact; use no pseudo-neuroscience diagram or numerical trust chart.
